## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A single-juan **Japanese Buddhist canonical-importation catalog**, the companion to **Saichō's** [KR6s0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6s/KR6s0105) *Tāizhōu lù*. This catalog documents the texts that Saichō received during the **Yuèzhōu** 越州 portion of his 805 return route from Tang China — particularly the **Esoteric** texts and rituals he received at **Lóngxīngsì** 龍興寺 in Yuèzhōu under the master **Shùnxiǎo** 順曉. Preserved at T55 no. 2160. See [KR6s0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6s/KR6s0105) for the principal substantive treatment of Saichō and his Tang mission.

**Abstract**

Authorship and date: composed by **Saichō** in **805 CE** immediately upon his return to Japan, complementing [KR6s0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6s/KR6s0105). *notBefore* = **805**, *notAfter* = **805**. Catalog dynasty 日本.

The Yuè-zhōu portion of Saichō's mission is significant for the **Esoteric** content: at Lóng-xīng-sì he received Esoteric initiation under **Shùn-xiǎo** 順曉, including ritual transmissions and *dhāraṇī* texts that became the foundational Esoteric component of the **Tendai-Shingon** integration that characterizes the Tendai school's doctrinal-ritual structure (in contrast to the more strictly Esoteric **Shingon** lineage of **Kūkai**, who received his Esoteric transmission directly from **Huì-guǒ** 惠果, the eighth Esoteric patriarch in Cháng-ān).

The two Saichō catalogs ([KR6s0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6s/KR6s0105) + [KR6s0106](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6s/KR6s0106)) together document the **complete inventory** of Saichō's 804–805 Tang study mission — totaling some **460 texts** (per the combined counts of the two catalogs).
